stories.head: G2's CPTO: AI agents now build B2B shortlists using third-party evidence, not vendor positioning
stories.plain: G2's chief product and technology officer explains that AI agents doing B2B research trust third-party reviews and structured evidence over a vendor's own marketing copy. This reshapes how software is bought: if an AI agent can't find credible external signals about your product, you won't make the shortlist — a direct threat to traditional demand-gen tactics.

stories.head: Adobe brings agentic AI to content supply chain with CX Enterprise Coworker in GenStudio
stories.plain: Adobe's CX Enterprise Coworker is an agentic teammate embedded in GenStudio that can orchestrate content creation, approval, and delivery workflows with human oversight. This matters because it moves AI from a copy-drafting helper to an autonomous operator inside enterprise content pipelines, changing how brands buy and govern creative production at scale.

stories.head: Zingtree launches agentic governance platform for contact centers in regulated industries
stories.plain: Zingtree targets healthcare, insurance, and financial services with a platform that lets companies govern and orchestrate AI agents handling high-stakes customer support. It adds controls over cost, latency, and decision boundaries — exactly the guardrails regulators and risk teams demand before autonomous agents can be deployed in sensitive customer interactions.

stories.head: From journeys to decisions: real-time AI decisioning replaces static customer journey maps
stories.plain: A MarTech Conference recap arguing that pre-built journey maps are too rigid for today's buyers and that real-time AI decisioning — choosing the next best action per person at the moment of contact — is the practical replacement. Useful framing for teams evaluating CEP vendors or rearchitecting their engagement stack.

stories.head: Claritas Email Advantage applies AI optimization to subject lines and audiences while campaigns run
stories.plain: Claritas's new acquisition email product adjusts audience targeting and subject lines dynamically during a live campaign, then uses holdout groups to measure whether changes actually lifted results. That closed feedback loop — test, adjust, measure — brings bandit-style optimization to email acquisition, a channel that has historically relied on static A/B tests run before send.

stories.head: G2's CPTO: AI agents now build B2B shortlists, trusting third-party evidence over vendor positioning
stories.plain: G2's chief product and technology officer explains how AI purchasing agents are replacing human researchers in B2B software buying — and that they cite third-party reviews and evidence, not vendor marketing copy. This fundamentally changes how marketing teams need to think about brand presence and generative engine visibility in the buying process.

stories.head: Adobe brings agentic AI to the content supply chain with CX Enterprise Coworker in GenStudio
stories.plain: Adobe's CX Enterprise Coworker is an agentic teammate embedded inside GenStudio that can orchestrate content creation and delivery at scale. It signals a major shift in how enterprise marketing teams will build, approve, and distribute personalized content — with an AI agent handling steps that previously required human coordination across multiple tools.

stories.head: Zingtree launches agentic governance and orchestration platform for regulated contact centers
stories.plain: Zingtree's new platform lets healthcare, insurance, and financial services companies deploy AI agents in customer support while keeping human-defined guardrails in place. It addresses the hardest problem in agentic AI adoption: how do you let agents act autonomously while staying compliant in regulated industries? This sets a template for governed agentic deployment.

stories.head: From journeys to decisions: real-time AI decisioning replaces static customer journey maps
stories.plain: A MarTech Conference session makes the case that static journey maps are obsolete — modern AI can make per-person, per-moment decisions about what to send, when, and on which channel. This reframes how marketing teams should evaluate CEPs and shifts budget thinking from campaign orchestration to real-time decisioning infrastructure.

stories.head: Claritas Email Advantage adds live AI optimization — adjusting audiences and subject lines while campaigns run
stories.plain: Claritas's new acquisition email product uses AI to adjust audience targeting and subject lines in real time during a live campaign, then measures actual lift using holdout groups. This moves email from a set-and-send channel to a continuously learning one — a meaningful shift in how marketers buy and evaluate email optimization tools.

themes.head: AI Agents Are Rewriting the Buyer Shortlist
body: AI agents — not human researchers — are increasingly doing the first round of vendor evaluation, pulling from third-party review sites, structured data, and public signals rather than your own positioning pages. G2's CPTO Alexis Zheng spelled out the implication plainly: brands that don't show up in AI-readable evidence won't make the consideration set, regardless of how good their own copy is.

This shifts marketing investment from polished owned-media messaging toward building verifiable, third-party-cited credibility. Tools like SEOAST's GEO & AEO audits and Marcora's brand-context layer for ChatGPT & Claude are early infrastructure responses — but most marketing teams haven't restructured their content strategy around this reality yet.

themes.head: Agentic AI Enters the Content Supply Chain
body: Adobe's CX Enterprise Coworker and its expanded Firefly Creative Studio represent a step-change: AI is no longer just a generation tool but an autonomous coworker that plans, drafts, reviews, and routes content across the full supply chain. Paired with the Adobe–Google model partnership, this creates end-to-end agentic workflows that compress multi-day creative cycles into hours.

The practical consequence for marketing teams is that human roles shift toward briefing, governance, and final approval rather than production. Medeo's white-label AI video platform and Zingtree's agentic governance layer for contact centers show the same pattern spreading across verticals — autonomy with guardrails is becoming the design standard.
ev: MarTech Series · Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker

themes.head: AI Traffic Is High-Intent but Structurally Different
body: Data now shows AI-referred visitors generate 83% more revenue per visit than average web traffic — but ChatGPT's paid traffic is worth far less than Google's equivalent. The divergence reveals a nuanced reality: AI channels deliver warm, decision-ready users when the query is organic and informational, but monetization models for AI-driven paid placements remain immature.

For multi-location and B2B brands, local AI visibility is emerging as a distinct discipline separate from traditional SEO. Marketers need separate tracking, separate content strategies, and separate attribution models for AI-referred sessions — combining tools like MMM with post-purchase surveys is one practical bridge until cleaner AI attribution infrastructure exists.
ev: MarTech · ChatGPT paid traffic vs Google
MarTech · Local AI visibility for multi-location brands

themes.head: Measurement Is Fragmenting Into Layers
body: A cluster of pieces this month converges on a single uncomfortable truth: no single measurement method works across all channels or time horizons. MMM captures long-run brand effects; post-purchase surveys capture last-touch intent; real-time optimization (like Claritas Email Advantage) handles in-flight decisions. Each lens answers a different question, and conflating them produces bad calls.

The practical response is a layered measurement stack rather than a unified attribution platform — right model for the right decision. Supermetrics' Campaign Manager, which pairs AI insights with campaign execution in one interface, points toward tooling that lets teams switch analytical frames without switching platforms, reducing the cognitive overhead of running multiple models simultaneously.
ev: MarTech · MMM with post-purchase survey attribution

themes.head: AI Productivity Gains Need Deliberate ROI Conversion
body: Efficiency gains from AI are real but they don't automatically translate to business outcomes — teams that save time on content production often just fill that time with more content rather than higher-value thinking. The month's editorial consensus is that converting productivity into ROI requires explicit redeployment decisions: fewer headcount additions, faster test-and-learn cycles, or reinvestment in strategy work.

Complicating this is the decentralization pressure AI creates inside marketing orgs — individual teams deploying their own AI tools fragment data, governance, and brand context. Martech platform buyers now need to audit AI context handling before signing contracts, and tools that inject consistent brand context (like Marcora's shared context layer) are addressing the organizational coherence problem that raw productivity tools leave behind.

month.takeaway: The month's signal is unified: AI is no longer a feature layer on top of existing martech — it is restructuring who discovers brands, who creates content, how performance is measured, and where organizational authority sits, forcing marketers to redesign strategy, tooling, and governance simultaneously.
